properties.name: Wae Rebo
properties.summary: Cone-shaped mbaru niang houses reached by a ~9 km forest trail; UNESCO Asia-Pacific heritage award.
properties.cultural_protocol: Guests received by elders; small donation and guest book expected; village council agreement required for the race.

properties.name: Inerie
properties.summary: A near-perfect volcanic cone (2,245 m) rising above the Ngada megalithic villages; a hike-a-bike shoulder traverse is on the table for the Ultra variant.
properties.story:
Inerie stands over Bena, Luba, Tololela and Gurusina like a stage backdrop — every one of the Ngada villages is arranged so a ceremony faces it. The **shoulder traverse** from the Bena side down to the arak-distilling coast at Aimere is steep, loose volcanic soil with real exposure; scouts have not yet confirmed it is safe with a loaded bike. See [the route concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inerie) for the full write-up.

Open questions before this goes in the course:
- Is the shoulder descent safe with a bike, loaded, in the dry season?
- Is a full circuit a safer substitute for the Ultra variant?
properties.hazard_level: Dormant — no current PVMBG alert, but re-check before the race (status as of this writing is from memory, not a dated bulletin).
